steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: The group has two parameters: the hull thickness in mm and the core layer skip n (1 to 10). FLAGS.OPT_OFF makes it optional and switched off, so by default the whole volume gets the volume hatch, as on the left.

lines: // Off by default. min_hull_thickness (mm): wall thickness of the hull;
// core_every_nth_layer: the core is exposed every n-th layer (1 = every
// layer). MPBF background: a thicker effective layer in the core saves
// time, the hull keeps the fine layers for an accurate surface.

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: The profile values are copied into the plain settings object part.hull_core. Everything after this point works with enabled, min_thickness and core_every_nth.

steps.title: Tell ATU before the layers are built
notes: Hull and core is a model feature: ATU prepares data for it before any layer is calculated. declareSingleHullCore registers the two values under a parameter set name.
coreSkip is the n of the section on the left: the core is exposed on every second layer here.

lines: // coreSkip: expose the core every n-th layer (1 = every layer);
// minThickness: minimum hull wall thickness in mm.

steps.title: Split the volume into hull and core
notes: For every volume area of a layer, the generator with the same parameter set name cuts off the hull. needCoreExposure answers whether this is a core layer.
On the other layers the core stays empty: layer 7 on the left has a hull only, the powder in the core waits for layer 8.

lines: // The generator is created for the current layer with the settings
// that were declared under this name (hull thickness, core skip).
// needCoreExposure() answers: "is this a layer where the core is exposed?"
return { hull: l_hull, core: l_core, core_active: l_active };

steps.title: Two hatches, two vector types
notes: The hull is hatched with the volume settings (BSID 500), the core with its own hatch group (BSID 510), but only when core_active is true. Without hull and core, the whole volume counts as hull.

lines: // Without hull / core the whole volume is "hull" (volume hatch).
let l_split = { hull: l_vol_area, core: ISL.empty(), core_active: false };
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_split.hull, l_part.hatching.volume, BSID.hatch_volume, l_id, l_b, false);
// core_active is false on layers where the core is skipped (core
// every n-th layer): then nothing is exposed in the core area.
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_split.core, l_part.hatching.core, BSID.hatch_core, l_id, l_b, false);

steps.title: Faster settings for the core
notes: The core is hidden inside the part, so it may use more productive settings: 350 W at 1300 mm/s and 0.12 mm hatch distance instead of 280 W, 1200 mm/s and 0.1 mm for the volume.
These are defaults: change them per profile under Scanning and Hatching › Core hatching.

lines: // The core uses a larger hatch distance (0.12 mm) by default: the core
// is not visible, so faster settings are acceptable there.

recipes.title: Switch hull and core on by default
recipes.why: New profiles split every volume into hull and core.
recipes.result: In a new profile, “Hull and core” shows on. Profiles you already have may keep their stored setting.

recipes.title: A 2 mm hull by default
recipes.why: A thicker shell with the volume settings, as in the video.
recipes.result: The default hull thickness is 2 mm. Move the hull slider in Try it to compare. For one profile, type the value in the dialog instead.

recipes.title: Expose the core every second layer
recipes.why: Saves build time in large solid parts.
recipes.result: The core then melts two layers of powder at once. The laser settings do not change by themselves: at 350 W the core gets about 37 J/mm³ instead of 75 J/mm³ (350 / (1300 · 0.12 · 0.06)), so check the core power too.

recipes.title: A coarser core hatch
recipes.why: Fewer lines in the core, faster build.
recipes.result: Core hatch about 64 J/mm³ instead of 75 J/mm³ per 30 µm layer (350 / (1300 · 0.14 · 0.03)).

recipes.title: More core power
recipes.why: More energy for the core, for example together with a core layer skip.
recipes.result: Core hatch default 380 W: about 81 J/mm³ per 30 µm layer. For one profile, change Scanning › Core hatching › power in the dialog instead.
